::: {.page-lede}
My teaching goal is to help students move from applying statistical procedures to making **defensible research decisions** across design, measurement, modeling, diagnostics, uncertainty, interpretation, and reproducible communication.
:::

<div class="teaching-service-jump" aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#teaching-philosophy">Teaching &amp; Mentoring</a><a href="#academic-service">Academic Service</a></div>

## Teaching Philosophy

Effective quantitative work combines technical execution with judgment about what a design and dataset can support. I teach statistical methods within a broader sequence of inquiry: define the research question, understand the data structure, choose a model the data can support, examine assumptions and diagnostics, interpret uncertainty, and communicate conclusions responsibly.

## Teaching Approach

::: {.teaching-approach-grid}
::: {.teaching-approach-card}
<div class="interest-label">01</div>
### Authentic Inquiry
I use real research problems to connect statistical technique with substantive reasoning. Code is a tool for quantitative thinking, not an end in itself.
:::

::: {.teaching-approach-card}
<div class="interest-label">02</div>
### Scaffolding & Feedback
I use conceptual explanations, worked examples, annotated code, structured decision prompts, and iterative feedback while maintaining common expectations for methodological reasoning.
:::

::: {.teaching-approach-card}
<div class="interest-label">03</div>
### Reproducible Practice
Students should leave a methods course able to produce an analysis that another researcher can understand, reproduce, and critique, with transparent workflows, diagnostic checks, and clear reporting of uncertainty.
:::
:::

<div class="teaching-service-divider" aria-hidden="true"></div>
